title: Commercial Requests Routing and Cost Allocation Triage Playbook
creator: Anika Patel
description: Playbook for intake, routing, and prioritization of commercial non-bug requests related to pricing, commitments, invoicing, cost allocation, and marketplace flows. Purpose: reduce triage time, standardize decisions that affect revenue recognition and billing implementation, and provide clear escalation paths to Finance, Legal, Sales, and Engineering.
triage_steps: 1) Intake channel identification: support ticket, AE intake form (Salesforce/HubSpot), product feedback board, or direct email to commercial-requests@redwood.com

2) Minimum required fields: customer name, account ID, contract reference (if any), requested outcome (commitment/invoice/marketplace change/cost allocation), estimated ARR impact, requested timeline, supporting documents (contracts/POs), requester role
3) Automated enrichment: attach account tier, billing model, current outstanding invoices, and last invoice date via Finance API
4) Initial triage (within 48h): PM owner assigns a severity and routes to Finance or Legal for compliance review if revenue recognition or contract changes are involved
5) Decision: Approve for standard handling / Escalate for custom implementation / Defer / Reject with next steps
6) If custom implementation, create product ticket and identify engineering scope and cost estimate, or coordinate with Dedicated/Private ops for provisioning changes
prioritization_criteria: Revenue risk: potential to create or protect ARR (weight 30%)
Compliance & contracts: legal complexity or need for audit trails (weight 20%)
Customer criticality: strategic account or escalation from AE/CS (weight 20%)
Implementation effort: engineering + finance effort estimates (weight 15%)
Frequency / scale: one-off vs repeatable vs platform change impacting many customers (weight 10%)
Time sensitivity: contractual deadline or renewal window (weight 5%)
decision_matrix_example: Score each incoming request 0-5 for each criterion, multiply by weights above, sum. Thresholds: >=4.0 proceed immediately; 2.5-4.0 schedule in next sprint or finance change; <2.5 low priority or handled by Sales/CS with playbook.
stakeholders: PM: triage owner and proposal owner
Finance: invoice generation, revenue recognition, GL mapping
Customer Success: change comms and handoff
Engineering: API or billing system integrations
Platform/Marketplace team: marketplace billing flows and connector updates
routing_rules: If request affects invoice numbers or GL mapping -> route to Finance + PM
If request requires contract amendment or new commercial terms -> route to Legal + Finance + Sales
If request is marketplace listing or billing modality (marketplace payout, marketplace invoice change) -> route to Marketplace team + Finance
If request demands per-tenant cost allocation or new cost-center tagging -> route to Engineering + Finance for API/workflow changes
If request is pricing configuration change with broad customer impact -> route to Product Pricing Committee and schedule cross-functional review
service_level_agreements: Initial decision or triage note: 5 business days
Finance/legal review for standard amendments: 10 business days
Implementation estimate from Eng: 2 sprints (or a clearly stated ETA)
Urgent contractual deadlines: treated as P0 and escalated to on-call PM, on-call finance partner, and sales leadership
examples: Example A - Committed capacity discount: AE requests a 6-month committed GPU capacity discount. Triage outcome: route to Finance for revenue recognition guidance, PM to assess runtime capacity changes, Eng to estimate quota enforcement work. Priority: high due to ARR impact.

Example B - Marketplace chargeback request: Marketplace partner reports incorrect fee allocation for July. Triage outcome: Marketplace + Finance investigate, create back-billing plan and customer-facing credit. Priority: medium (time-bound), requires legal review if contract clause applies.

Example C - Cost-center tagging API: Ops team requests tag-by-cost-center billing export for internal chargeback. Triage outcome: Eng to add export endpoint, Finance to map GL codes; scheduled as P2 platform change. Priority: low-medium but repeatable; flagged for Optimize roadmap
escalation_paths: If Finance identifies revenue recognition risk -> escalate to Head of Finance and Legal
If request impacts SLA or Dedicated capacity -> escalate to Ops/Infrastructure lead
If cross-functional alignment stalls for >7 business days -> schedule decision forum with PM, Sales lead, Head of Finance, and Head of Engineering
metrics_and_reporting: Number of back-billing or invoicing corrections per quarter
open_questions_and_decisions: Should we centralize intake in HubSpot or keep multi-channel with auto-enrichment? (PM recommendation: centralize eventually but accept multi-channel during transition)
What is the SLA Finance can commit to for contract amendments? (Finance: 10 business days unless expedited)
Do marketplace changes require a separate cadence and committee? (Proposed: quarterly marketplace ops review for non-urgent changes)
